newsitem.title: CONGO: Troops deploy around Congo ex-president's home.
newsitem.headline: Troops deploy around Congo ex-president's home.

text.p: The Congolese army on Thursday deployed troops and armoured cars in the capital around the home of former president Denis Sassou Nguesso, whose supporters have been involved in clashes in the north.
Witnesses said at least six armoured cars had deployed at about 4 a.m. (0300 GMT) in Brazzaville's northeastern Mpila district.
There was no immediate official comment on the deployments but a government statement on Wednesday night threatened tough measures against anyone found carrying an unauthorised weapon.
Residents said the deployment was followed by automatic weapons fire. The district was closed to traffic and soldiers were searching pedestrians.

"Since five o'clock this morning there has been sustained shooting around my residence. There are about 10 armoured vehicles and infantry soldiers," Sassou Nguesso told Radio France Internationale. "One of my security men has already received bullet wounds in the shoulder."
The government is trying to crack down on private militias loyal to political leaders in the run-up to presidential election on July 27.

Clashes between supporters of Sassou Nguesso and former prime minister Jacques Joachim Yhombi Opango in the two leaders' northern home towns, Owando and Oyo, have killed 16 people in less than a month.
The government said it would pursue two senior members of Sassou Nguesso's guard whom it held responsible for the clashes.

Last Friday the government banned private militias and the unauthorised carrying of arms, and on Saturday party leaders meeting in Brazzaville pledged to avoid violence in any conflict arising from the election.

About a dozen candidates are expected to contest the elections. The three front-runners are President Pascal Lissouba, Sassou Nguesso and opposition leader Bernard Kolelas, 1992 runner-up and mayor of Brazzaville.

"I believe that, on the whole, the authorities want to create incidents to prevent the presidential elections from taking place because they are expected to be held in less than two months under normal circumstances," Sassou Nguesso said.
Political parties armed their supporters during ethnic and political fighting following parliamentary elections in 1993 that left 2,000 dead in Brazzaville.
Brazzaville is located just across the river from Kinshasa, capital of the Democratic Republic of Congo, formerly Zaire.
